podcast.body: This song was Kansas's only Top 10 hit, reaching number six in April 1978. Written by Kerry Livgren, it draws references from the Bible, specifically Ecclesiastes ("everything he has accomplished is futile, like chasing the wind") and Genesis ("for dust thou art, and unto dust thou shalt return"). Some clergy members rejected the song's message due to the line "all we are is dust in the wind," deeming it potentially offensive. The song's universal theme of the impermanence of life resonated widely. "Dust in the wind, number six, in April 1978, the one and only top ten hit for Kansas."
